propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate implemented SDK changes for a payments company's checkout SDK for three years against the API team's specifications under the SDK engineering standard, each on a pull request in his name, and wrote the SDK's automated tests and reviewed merchant-facing sample code as one of the team's reviewers.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the pull requests document the changes, the tests and the reviews.

propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate supported the merchants' engineers through the developer forum with the referral split marked, took each change through the review and release process with the release approval recorded as the SDK lead's, and wrote the limitation note and hand-over conditions of each release.
propositions.rationale: The resume and the work sample document the forum support, the release process and the release records.

propositions.canonicalProposition: The candidate can lead the SDK's technical direction across the two SDK teams, as shown by the interviewer's impression that he operated at a senior level and is brilliant.
propositions.rationale: The interviewer note records praise and an impression of seniority, not an observed technical leadership event; the materials document engineering work on one team and no technical plan or direction-setting across teams.

expectedGap: The materials document engineering work on one SDK team; they do not document a technical plan or technical direction set across teams.
expectedBoundaryNote: Record the interviewer's praise as a signal to verify with a concrete example; do not present an impression of seniority as evidence for the technical direction requirement, which the materials leave undocumented.
permittedFollowUpTargets: Ask for any technical plan or architecture decision the candidate authored that more than one team built against.

signatures: mark the technical direction requirement as covered
